subject: Request: short‑lived prefetch debug flag for BrightLane POC
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Bell <paul.bell@brightlane.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short‑lived prefetch debug flag for BrightLane POC

Hi team —

Quick context: BrightLane is in the home stretch for next‑week POC demos. During last Friday’s run they hit repeated stalls that appear correlated with our prefetch path. They want a short‑lived, developer‑toggleable debug flag we can enable just for their demo traffic (no long lived opt in) so we can safely gather more observability and, if needed, flip to the safe path without a hotfix.

Ask: can Platform expose a runtime flag (preferably via route metadata or a header override) that: 
- turns on prefetch debug logging (KV cache entries, prefetch decisions),
- forces prefetch bypass for a single route (so we can compare), and
- is scoped to a route token or a small IP range for the demo?

Requirements:
- Demo window: 2028‑08‑28 09:00–11:00 PT (tight)
- Non‑prod pathway is acceptable but BrightLane wants no risk of degrading other customers
- We prefer a short TTL (30m) and an easy rollback UI or API call

Attached is a small repro set BrightLane sent (brightlane-repro-logs-20280821.zip) and a proposed patch idea (prefetch-debug-poc.patch) from their eng lead.

Next steps I’m proposing:
1) Platform confirms feasibility and preferred surface (header, route metadata, or admin toggle)
2) If possible, runtime ship a canary toggle we can enable for the demo
3) SalesEng will coordinate the rollout window and test with BrightLane SRE

Karthik/Marissa — any initial thoughts? If this is not feasible, we should prepare a fallback plan (e.g., dedicated canary node for BrightLane).

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
T: +1 415‑555‑0126
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Bell <paul.bell@brightlane.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short‑lived prefetch debug flag for BrightLane POC

On Tue, Aug 21, 2028 at 09:12 AM Tessa Morgan wrote:
> Quick context: BrightLane is in the home stretch for next‑week POC demos...

Thanks for the clear ask, Tessa. Short answer: doable, with caveats. Longer:

What I can provide quickly:
- A header toggle (x-rw-prefetch-mode: debug|bypass|default) is simplest from an API surface perspective and avoids new admin UX changes.
- We need to make sure the toggle is opt‑in per route token and rate limited — I can scope it to a token ID on the route metadata so only BrightLane’s token sees it.
- For logging, enabling debug will increase log volume; we should stream those logs to a temporary S3 bucket tied to the BrightLane repro run rather than increase global retention.

Questions / concerns:
1) Are we comfortable with a header-based escape hatch in hosted for a customer demo? It’s low friction but requires careful access control.
2) If BrightLane provided that patch, is it aligned to our runtime version? We’ll need the exact binary/commit they had when reproing.
3) I’ll need repro steps that reliably trigger the stall — token + example call + approximate QPS used during the failure. The attached logs help but I’ll follow up with what else I need.

If this meets the chart, I can scope a small canary that K8s ops can flip for a single node pool. Estimated work: 0.5–1.5 engineer days to add header parsing, scoping, and the ephemeral log sink.

Marissa — can you confirm any runtime safety checks we'd want (max debug TTL, enforcement of route token scoping) and whether a bypass path exists already we can reuse?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Bell <paul.bell@brightlane.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short‑lived prefetch debug flag for BrightLane POC

Karthik —

We do have a bypass path in the serving layer but it isn’t exposed as a customer‑facing header today; it’s gated behind an operator flag we flip during troubleshooting. Exposing a header is fine but we should add two safety features up front: 
1) TTL enforcement server‑side (hard cap 1 hour)
2) Token scoping —  the router will validate that the token belongs to a whitelisted customer for the flag.

Implementation approach I propose:
- Add x-rw-prefetch-mode header parsing at the edge router (low risk). Valid values: debug, bypass, unset.
- Router checks token against an allowlist (we’ll put BrightLane token ID in there for the window).
- Router emits structured debug events to a temporary S3 sink (brightlane-prefetch-debug-20280828) with a per‑file size cap. We’ll scrub PII by default.
- If bypass=on, router returns a metric tag so we can compare latency/cost delta in the A/B.

I attached a small patch that mocks header handling and a script to collect a minimal repro dataset (prefetch-debug-poc.patch). I can carve out a half day to land the header parsing + allowlist check; Karthik, if you can provision the canary node pool and short TTL enforcement, we should be able to enable this by 2028‑08‑26 and validate in staging.

Fallback plan: if we can’t land this in time, we’ll spin a dedicated canary node pool that routes BrightLane traffic to a node with the operator flag enabled. That’s higher ops overhead but avoids any surface changes.

Marissa Cole
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachments: prefetch-debug-poc.patch (text/patch), brightlane-repro-logs-20280821.zip (application/zip)

Subject: Re: Request: short‑lived prefetch debug flag for BrightLane POC

Paul — quick update for the demo schedule: Platform can support an x-rw-prefetch-mode header scoped to your token and limited TTL. Marissa and Karthik will land the header parsing + allowlist in staging and we’ll enable a canary node pool if anything blocks.

Action items for BrightLane: please send the exact token ID you’ll use for the demo and confirm the demo window (we have 08/28 09:00–11:00 PT penciled). Also let us know if you want us to stream the debug output to your S3 or a Redwood temporary bucket.

Thanks — we’ll keep this tight and revert the allowlist right after the demo.

Tessa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
